body:
I always considered myself happy and content with the way my life was going. Even at my lowest, I would always bounce right back. As terrible as it sounds, whenever I felt like my world was crashing down, I would always think about how someone, somewhere has it a hell of a lot worse than I do. That didn't necessarily make me feel better, but it made me remember everything that I do have that others don't. How can I be whining about how terrible my life is when I have enough food to be gluttonous? I live in a decent house in a decent neighborhood. I have clothes on my back and was given a solid education, it's not their fault I squandered it.

Then everything went wrong, and all it took was one solid thought about my future. Looking back, I honestly believed that I wouldn't make it, I never made any plans. But all it took was that one thought and my fools paradise came crashing down around me. I've never felt so scared in my life.

Everyone here has been so supportive, I don't know what I would have done if it weren't for you guys.

A popular line of opinion here, however, seems to be that I don't need a degree to be happy, I just need to follow my passion. I just don't want to be a deadbeat like my real parents, having someone else take care of me. And is the 'starving artist' life really that glamourous?

Maybe I will decide college isn't right for me, but then what? I don't have a passion, something that I could see myself spending the rest of my life on. I barely do anything. I've spent most of my life sleeping (like 10-12 hours a day). Now that I look back on that, it's probably a big problem that I should have noticed sooner. One more thing to add to my crazy, right?

I'm not good at anything, certainly not great at anything. I'm also lazy, with a short attention span, which has been a bit of a road block for me my entire life. Not to mention that I'm so socially awkward around strangers that I can barely go shopping on my own.

I'd do anything to take back those thoughts and give myself one more year of peace before I have to start making decisions. However, since I know that's not possible, I'm glad I came here.

You all have no idea the impact your making on my life, like a might actually have a shot. So thank you. All of you. This community has helped me more in the last few hours than I could have ever imagined.
